subject: Annual Black History Month Assembly
overview: The Medford High School Black Student Union hosted an assembly featuring guest speakers and student performances to celebrate the history and culture of the African American community.

items.title: Welcome and Opening Remarks
items.summary: Student leaders Melissa Antoine and others opened the assembly by introducing the program of speeches, dances, and cultural events.

items.title: Performance of the Black National Anthem
items.summary: A student performed "Lift Every Voice and Sing" following a historical overview of the hymn's origins with the NAACP.

items.title: Black Student Union Opening Dance
items.summary: Members of the Black Student Union performed a choreographed opening dance routine for the assembly.

items.title: Mayor's Address on Local Black History
items.summary: Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn spoke about Medford’s historical ties to the Underground Railroad and recognized local figures such as Edward Duggar and Belinda Sutton.

items.title: Soca Dance Performance
items.summary: Students performed a Soca dance, which speakers described as a blend of African and East Indian rhythms.

items.title: Superintendent's Remarks on Change Agents
items.summary: Superintendent Dr. Marice Edouard-Vincent highlighted historical Medford residents who acted as change agents, including Prince Hall and Elizabeth Oliver Newton.

items.title: Guest Speaker Brian Owens
items.summary: Guest speaker Brian Owens shared his experiences as a retail executive and student-athlete, emphasizing the importance of education and personal branding.

items.title: Tribute to Ashley Berners-Woods
items.summary: Alumni presented a poem and artwork in memory of former student-athlete Ashley Berners-Woods.

items.title: Poetry and Fashion Show
items.summary: Student Chris Xavier performed a poem about the Black experience in America, followed by a fashion show featuring traditional African clothing and historical eras.

items.title: Closing Remarks and Acknowledgments
items.summary: The event concluded with thanks to the Black Student Union advisors and participating speakers.
